back: The price level and real output at which AD equals short-run aggregate supply.

front: What happens to output, price level and employment when AD shifts right?
back: All three rise (demand-pull); the nearer to potential output, the more the price level rises.

front: What happens when SRAS shifts left?
back: The price level rises, output and employment fall (cost-push, stagflation).

front: What happens when SRAS shifts right?
back: The price level falls, output and employment rise.
Inflation occurring together with falling output and rising unemployment, typically after a leftward shift of SRAS.
Demand-pull: a rise in the price level from a rightward shift of AD. Cost-push: a rise in the price level from a leftward shift of SRAS (higher costs).

front: Why does spare capacity matter when AD rises?
back: With spare capacity SRAS is shallow, so output rises with little price rise; near potential output SRAS is steep, so mostly prices rise.

front: How do you describe an AD/AS diagram in words?
back: Name the axes, the curves and the original equilibrium, state the shift, give the new equilibrium and the changes in price level, output and employment.
